title: S&P Global US Services PMI (final, Sep 2026 data) — 09:45 ET, 15 minutes before ISM Services
source: EST: rule-derived from S&P Global's OWN published cadence, read verbatim off pmi.spglobal.com/Public/Release/ReleaseDates?language=en (fetched direct 2026-09-09, HTTP 200): "The standard monthly release schedules for S&P Global PMI surveys are as follows: Manufacturing PMI: first working day / Services PMI: third working day / Whole Economy PMI: third working day." October 2026 opens on a Thursday, so its first three working days are Thu 10-01, Fri 10-02 and Mon 10-05 — the same derivation that ISM's own third-business-day rule produces for ism-services-2026-10-05, and the same one that reproduced all nine 2026 ISM release dates with nothing left over. The 09:45 ET time is S&P Global's published US PMI slot: the same calendar page lists 'S&P Global Flash US PMI' at 13:45 UTC on 2026-09-23, and 13:45 UTC is 09:45 ET under EDT. FILED estimate on three counts, none of which is doubt about the date: this lane never self-confirms an event it discovered in-sweep; market-events-data.ts defines no confirmed-source prefix covering a private PMI compiler (IR:/CAL:/BLS:/FED:/TSY:/BEA:/CENSUS:/ISM:/CB:/PJM:/SEC:/OCC: all miss — the same standing schema gap the ISM entries and the funding-deadline ledger have both named); and the October row was NOT read off the calendar listing itself, which truncated before it and then rate-limited to HTTP 202 with an empty body on five retries from two user agents (recorded in the proposing ledger's probe-ref.blocked, not worked around). The DATE is a rule application, not a listing — say so before citing it
notes: PROPOSED AS A STRUCTURAL CONTAMINANT, NOT AS A TRADEABLE PRINT — and it closes a whole-publisher gap: this calendar tracks ZERO S&P Global PMI entries while tracking six ISM ones, even though S&P Global publishes a competing survey of the SAME reference month, on the SAME third-working-day cadence, FIFTEEN MINUTES AHEAD of ISM at 09:45 ET. That matters here because two registered forward tests measure the ISM release at intraday resolution using a window that contains this release and has never named it: FT-48 (owned by ism-services-2026-12-03, PASSED 2026-09-04) ranks the 09:30-10:30 ET bar for the ETFs and 09:20-10:20 for ^TNX, and FT-ism-services-2026-11-04-1 (owned by ism-services-2026-11-04, registered 2026-09-08) is scored on the 10-05 print with a named-contaminant void clause that does not name this. Neither score is retracted by this proposal — an unnamed contaminant inside a window is a limit to state, not a result to reverse — but every future intraday test of an ISM Services release should name this print in its void clause, and the 09:45 slot is why the 'release hour' has been measured to be QUIETER than an ordinary hour in four of five instruments if the information is already half-priced by 10:00. Read it, do not trade it, on the same measured grounds as its ISM sibling: the flash version of this same survey publishes ~2 weeks earlier (2026-09-23 on the fetched calendar), so the final revision is the least surprising services datum of the month, and this calendar has measured the LOUDER ISM print to nil across nine releases at daily resolution and one at intraday. Cheap falsifier, dated and self-adjudicating in ~3 weeks: S&P Global's own release-dates page will list October once the rate limit clears, and the 10-01 Manufacturing PMI (first working day, same rule) tests the cadence three sessions earlier at zero cost. Discovered during the ism-services-2026-10-05 pulse check (2026-09-09).
